question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` ever expose internal OpenClaw tool calls, and if so should that be a redacted opt-in diagnostic surface rather than OpenAI `tool_calls`?
rationale: Current code and docs deliberately model OpenAI `tool_calls` as caller-supplied client tools, while internal OpenClaw tool arguments can include sensitive operator context and would create a new public API/security contract.

options.title: Keep Current Boundary
options.body: Continue returning OpenAI-compatible `tool_calls` only for caller-supplied client tools and point internal-tool debugging to existing or future diagnostic surfaces.

options.title: Design Redacted Diagnostic Mode
options.body: Add a separate opt-in, scoped, redacted internal-tool telemetry contract after specifying what fields can be exposed and to whom.

options.title: Expose Internal Calls As tool_calls
options.body: Map internal OpenClaw tool calls into Chat Completions responses, accepting the compatibility and sensitive-data burden of that API contract.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Boundary
recommendation.body: Continue returning OpenAI-compatible `tool_calls` only for caller-supplied client tools and point internal-tool debugging to existing or future diagnostic surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced the original Gateway HTTP endpoint and landed the client-tool protocol follow-up, so it is the strongest history signal for the API boundary decision.
